schemeScope: Combined Ordinary scheme (12 pages). PDF 1 cover; 2 blank; 3 general marking instruction (red ink, major errors underlined) and Páipéar I Ceist 1 composition marking (tariffs Tasc 3, Ábhar 9, Cumas Gaeilge 48 for each of two pieces, “= 60 marc × 2 = 120 marc”; the bracketed Cumas Gaeilge definition; the bracketed content note; the examiner’s Nóta; a bracketed Nóta on “Gaeilge Lochtach”); 4 Ceist 2 reading (each question restated with one price, no answers; a 0–5 language deduction for each passage; B’s closing note on redundancy and language); 5–9 Páipéar II; 10 the listening test; 11 Socruithe Réasúnta; 12 empty.
reviewMethod: Every paper page (1 instructions, 2 composition, 3–4 reading, 5–8 “Leathanach Bán”) and every applicable scheme page read in the text layer and checked against the printed page. The reading pages are typeset in tiles whose edges repeat the boundary glyph in the text layer (“John Hum me”, “C Cén”); the builder reads each page glyph by glyph by origin, draws a repeated glyph once and keeps the two passage columns apart, and asserts every prompt, title and composition line against that reading. The scheme sets its multiplication sign (PDF 3, 5, 6, 8, 9) and its PDF 11 bullets in SymbolMT (U+F0B4, U+F0B7), read as × and •.

nonPoolDecisions: Páipéar I before 2012 is the composition and the reading (220); the listening test is a paper of its own (irish_ordinary_2011_aural.py).

Composition: each of the nine printed titles is one 60-mark card (Tasc 3, Ábhar 9, Cumas Gaeilge 48, as the scheme prices each of the two pieces); choose-two is a choice, not a route; no combination cards. The scheme prints no 48-mark table, so Cumas Gaeilge is judged on its printed aspects.

Reading: the scheme prints no answers, only each question’s asks restated and one 10-mark price; each question is one card with one 10-mark criterion claimed whole (0 or 10) and marked tariffOnly; no part is a practice card of its own, because the scheme prices no part on its own. The card says “The scheme prints no answer for this part.”
sourceFindings: Páipéar I = 220: composition 120 (any two of A–D at 60: Tasc 3, Ábhar 9, Cumas Gaeilge 48) and reading 100 (A John Hume and B Sinéad Ahearne, five questions each at 10).

Reading (PDF 4): each question restated with one price and no answer; B 2’s price is printed “= 10 mar”, kept as printed. One 0–5 language deduction for each passage, and B’s closing Nóta on redundancy (“Gearrfar pionós i ngeall ar iomarcaíocht.”); cards state them without applying them.
Composition (PDF 3): the examiner’s Nóta misprints “Tasc” as “Tásc”; kept as printed. No 48-mark table and no short-attempt columns.
The reading pages’ text layer is tiled (each tile repeats its boundary glyph); the printed page reads normally, and every carded line is read from glyph origins with each repeated glyph drawn once.
